about: Notable sporting moments by date (MM-DD). Used for 'this day / week / month in sporting history'.

items.text: The first Super Bowl: the Green Bay Packers beat the Kansas City Chiefs.
Torvill and Dean skate their Boléro at the Sarajevo Winter Olympics, earning a full set of perfect 6.0s for artistic impression.
The 'Miracle on Ice': the USA's college team beats the Soviet Union at the Lake Placid Winter Olympics.
'The Fight of the Century': Joe Frazier beats Muhammad Ali at Madison Square Garden.
The first ever Test match begins: Australia v England at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.
The first FA Cup final: Wanderers beat Royal Engineers 1–0 at Kennington Oval.
Red Rum wins the Grand National for a record third time.
Aldaniti and Bob Champion, who had recovered from cancer, win the Grand National.
The first modern Olympic Games open in Athens.
Tiger Woods, aged 21, wins the Masters by 12 shots for his first major title.
Tiger Woods wins his fifth Masters, 22 years after his first.
The first FA Cup final at Wembley, the 'White Horse Final': Bolton Wanderers beat West Ham United 2–0.
Leicester City, 5000–1 outsiders, are confirmed Premier League champions.
Roger Bannister runs the first sub-four-minute mile (3:59.4) at Iffley Road, Oxford.
Sergio Agüero's stoppage-time goal against QPR wins Manchester City the Premier League title.
The 'Miracle of Istanbul': Liverpool come from 3–0 down to beat AC Milan on penalties in the Champions League final.
Manchester United score twice in stoppage time to beat Bayern Munich 2–1 in the Champions League final.
Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay become the first climbers confirmed to reach the summit of Everest.
The first Oxford–Cambridge Boat Race is rowed at Henley. Oxford win.
Paul Gascoigne's famous volley helps England beat Scotland 2–0 at Euro 96.
Diego Maradona's 'Hand of God' and 'Goal of the Century' as Argentina beat England 2–1 at the Mexico World Cup.
South Africa win the Rugby World Cup on home soil; Nelson Mandela presents the trophy in Johannesburg.
The longest tennis match ever ends at Wimbledon: John Isner beats Nicolas Mahut 70–68 in the fifth set after 11 hours 5 minutes.
England lose their Euro 96 semi-final to Germany on penalties at Wembley.
England lose their Italia 90 semi-final to West Germany on penalties in Turin.
Arthur Ashe becomes the first Black man to win the Wimbledon singles title.
Boris Becker, aged 17, becomes Wimbledon's youngest men's singles champion.
Andy Murray wins Wimbledon, the first British man to take the title since Fred Perry in 1936.
The first Wimbledon Championships begin.
Spain win their first World Cup, beating the Netherlands 1–0 in Johannesburg.
England win the Cricket World Cup at Lord's on boundary count after a tied super over against New Zealand.
Nadia Comăneci, aged 14, scores the first perfect 10 in Olympic gymnastics in Montreal.
Bradley Wiggins becomes the first British rider to win the Tour de France.
The London 2012 Olympic Games open.
The 'Austerity Games': the London 1948 Olympics open at Wembley.
England win the World Cup, beating West Germany 4–2 after extra time at Wembley.
The Lionesses win Euro 2022, beating Germany 2–1 after extra time at Wembley.
Jesse Owens wins the 100 metres at the Berlin Olympics, the first of his four gold medals.
'Super Saturday': Jessica Ennis, Greg Rutherford and Mo Farah win Olympic gold within an hour in London.
The first Premier League matches are played.
Usain Bolt runs the 100 metres in 9.58 seconds in Berlin, still the world record.
England beat Germany 5–1 in Munich in a World Cup qualifier.
The Football League, the world's first, plays its first matches.
The 'Miracle at Medinah': Europe come from 10–6 down on the final day to win the Ryder Cup.
South Africa beat New Zealand 12–11 in Paris to win a record fourth Rugby World Cup.
'The Rumble in the Jungle': Muhammad Ali knocks out George Foreman in Kinshasa to regain the world heavyweight title.
South Africa beat England 32–12 in Yokohama to win the Rugby World Cup.
Jonny Wilkinson's extra-time drop goal wins England the Rugby World Cup against Australia in Sydney.
Hungary beat England 6–3 at Wembley, England's first home defeat by a team from continental Europe.
The first international football match: Scotland 0–0 England in Glasgow.
Argentina beat France on penalties after a 3–3 draw to win the World Cup in Qatar.
